description: PlatformHttpClient against a small HTTP/1.1 server the test runs on 127.0.0.1 (plan §9 HttpClient): URLSession, HttpClient, libsoup. The server's routes: /echo answers 200 with the JSON {method, path, header (the X-Test request header, or null), body (the request body as text)}; /status/<n> answers <n> with the body 'status <n>'; /slow waits 5 s, then answers 200; /redirect/<path> answers 302 to /<path> (the same origin); /redirect-to-localhost/<path> answers 302 to http://localhost:<port>/<path> (another origin: another host name); /big/<n> answers 200 with n bytes of x. given.url's <server> is the server's address (http://127.0.0.1:<port>); <closed> is a port nothing listens on. Any status is an answer; no answer is http.failed with the system's reason; a cancelled call is job.cancelled. Redirects are followed within the same origin only (the same host and port, or http to https on the same host): a redirect elsewhere is the answer, so the request's headers never reach another host. A body larger than 16 MiB (16777216 bytes) is http.failed. A URL that can't be parsed is http.failed, and no error quotes a URL (expect.reasonLacks).

expect.rule: the X-Test header (an API key, say) never goes to a host the request didn't name
